newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF welcomes Russian rouble move.
newsitem.headline: IMF welcomes Russian rouble move.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund welcomes Russia's announcement that it will redenominate the rouble next year as a sign of a maturing economy, the IMF resident representative in Moscow said on Monday.
"It's certainly an encouraging sign of the government's confidence in its ability to maintain low inflation," Martin Gilman told Reuters.
"It's more symbolic... In terms of economic fundamentals it doesn't change anything," he added.
Earlier President Boris Yeltsin said that from January 1, 1998, one new rouble would equal 1,000 old, wiping three zeroes off current roubles.
Gilman said the move, which was not an easy decision, would make transactions easier in the economy.
It was important the move be well prepared, and ordinary Russians be well educated about the change, he said. Announcing the change well in advance, as was done on Monday, was part of that process.
